"Battleship" is a 2012 science fiction film that follows a naval fleet on a training exercise in the Pacific Ocean. During their mission, they encounter an alien armada that has arrived on Earth after receiving a signal sent from a communication system in Hawaii. The aliens, resembling humanoid sea creatures, attempt to establish a power source on Earth by using the naval fleet's equipment.

The movie's protagonist, Alex Hopper, played by Liam Neeson, is a rebellious yet talented young officer who must rise to the occasion when his brother, Admiral Hopper, is incapacitated during the initial attack. Alex takes command of the USS John Paul Jones, a battleship, to lead the charge against the invading aliens.

With the Hawaiian islands under threat, the crew of the USS John Paul Jones must devise a strategy using their battleship game's tactics because their other advanced systems have been disabled. They enlist the help of a scientist, Samantha Shane, played by Rihanna, who deciphers the aliens' intentions and vulnerabilities. 

Throughout the film, Alex grapples with personal challenges and leadership dilemmas, ultimately leading his team in a high-stakes naval battle to save the world. In an epic showdown, they exploit the aliens' weakness to sunlight, incapacitating their forces and securing a victory for Earth. The film concludes with Alex being promoted for his bravery and strategic prowess.

"Battleship" is an action-packed film based on the classic board game, but it expands the concept into a full-fledged sci-fi adventure. The story takes place off the coast of Hawaii during a multinational naval exercise. When a group of aliens arrive and begin communicating through a series of mysterious signals, they inadvertently activate an ancient underwater device.

The human fleet, led by Lieutenant Alex Hopper, a skilled but cocky officer, and his more experienced sister, Lieutenant Stella Hopper, must work together to decipher the alien signals and prevent a full-scale invasion. As the aliens start to attack Earth with advanced technology, the naval forces realize that their only chance is to disable the device and cut off the aliens' power source.

Throughout the film, Alex learns the value of teamwork and leadership, while Stella plays a crucial role in developing a strategy to outmaneuver the aliens. The climax involves a daring mission where the humans use a combination of traditional naval tactics and innovative approaches to defeat the alien fleet and save the planet.

Battleship (2012) is a science fiction action film inspired by the Hasbro board game of the same name. The plot revolves around an international naval fleet encountering an alien armada in the Pacific Ocean.

The main character is Alex Hopper (played by Taylor Kitsch), a directionless young man who joins the U.S. Navy at his brother's insistence. During a series of naval exercises near Hawaii (RIMPAC), Earth makes contact with an alien species when their ships crash-land in the Pacific Ocean. These aliens establish a force field around parts of the Hawaiian Islands and begin a hostile campaign against Earth.

The aliens, who are technologically advanced, engage in battle with the naval fleet. The story follows Hopper and his fellow sailors as they fight to prevent the aliens from establishing a communications array that would allow them to call for reinforcements to invade Earth. The naval forces must use strategy, conventional weapons, and their ships to combat the alien threat.

The film includes various nods to the original board game, including scenes where the naval officers must use a tracking system similar to the game's grid-based gameplay to locate and attack alien vessels. The movie culminates in a final battle between human and alien forces, with Earth's military forces fighting to save the planet from invasion.

The film stars Taylor Kitsch, Alexander Skarsgård, Rihanna, Brooklyn Decker, and Liam Neeson.

"Battleship" is a 2012 science fiction action film loosely based on the classic board game. The plot follows Alex Hopper, a disobedient U.S. Navy lieutenant, who is stationed aboard the USS Missouri during the RIMPAC naval exercises. The peaceful exercises take a dramatic turn when Earth is invaded by a massive fleet of advanced extraterrestrial warships, which had been attracted to the planet by powerful signals sent into deep space from the islands of Hawaii.

As the alien ships form an impenetrable shield around the Hawaiian Islands, isolating the RIMPAC fleet from the rest of the world, the young officer must reluctantly take command of his destroyer. Hopper and his crew face off against the alien invaders using clever tactics, including mimicking movements similar to the strategic format of the Battleship board game, to outmaneuver the technologically superior adversaries.

With the help of a few old veterans aboard their museum-ship-turned-combatant, Hopper and his team engage in a climactic battle and manage to defeat the alien leader, thereby dismantling the shield, saving the Earth, and restoring peace. In a gripping finale, a twist occurs when the Secretary of Defense reveals that the extraterrestrial ships were actually automated probes sent by a distant galactic civilization to assess Earth's military capabilities.
